mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE is low, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases when HOUST > 1300, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic output, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO is increasing, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) outpaces inflation (CPIAUCSL), it indicates a healthy economy, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 growth > CPIAUCSL growth, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when RSAFS > 720000, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS is increasing, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high, it may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE > 4.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is falsified.
